title: Infra GPU Fleet & Capacity — Cloud Accounts, Networking, IaC Modules, CI/CD (Team Wiki Integration Guide)
author: Alex Martinez
body:
Summary
-------
This team wiki page consolidates the operational playbooks, IaC module guidance, CI/CD conventions, cloud account structure, and networking requirements for Redwood Inference's GPU fleet. The goal is to provide a single integration reference for infra engineers onboarding to GPU capacity work, cross-team reviewers (SRE, serving runtime, security), and automation owners.

Goals
-----
- Define a repeatable, secure cloud account and VPC topology for GPU capacity.
- Standardize Terraform modules and usage patterns for fleet provisioning.
- Describe CI/CD pipelines and build artifacts that manage GPU infra lifecycles.
- Document runbooks for scaling, incident response, and maintenance windows.
- Provide ownership, SLAs, and a rollout checklist for changes.

Scope and Audience
------------------
This document applies to: infra engineers, platform SREs, the serving-runtime team that consumes GPUs, and the security team auditing account networking. It covers AWS (primary), with notes for GCP/Azure equivalents where relevant. This is not a low-level service design doc — see related pages for module reference and runbooks.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Primary owners: infra/gpu-capacity team (oncall: infra-oncall@redwood.example.com)
- Architecture reviewer: Jordan Lee (serving-runtime)
- Security reviewer: Priya Patel (security)
- Change approval: Fleet capacity review board (weekly cadence)

High-level Architecture
-----------------------
- Cloud account layout: org-root -> billing -> infra-shared-services -> gpu-prod, gpu-staging, gpu-dev.
- Networking: Shared Services account hosts centralized Transit Gateway and firewall appliances. Each GPU account has a VPC per-region (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1) with standardized subnetting and route tables.
- Provisioning: Terraform modules in the infra repo provision accounts, VPCs, ENIs, IAM roles, and instance/node pools. CI/CD pipelines apply changes via an automation account with limited cross-account role.

SLOs and Capacity Targets
-------------------------
- Latency SLOs (service-level): 95th-percentile request latency <= configured target per model (runtime teams set model SLOs). Infra SLO: instance boot time for autoscaling < 4 minutes (target) / < 10 minutes (max).
- Availability target for Dedicated GPU pools: 99.9% monthly.
- Buffer strategy: maintain 20% spare capacity per region for production during business hours. For Q4 and large launches increase buffer to 30% and prewarm nodes 24-72h in advance.

Capacity Planning Process (high-level)
-------------------------------------
1. Demand signal: product/serving runtime produces 30-day forecast and 7-day spike plan.
2. Infra analysis: run job-level simulations (batch and online), convert to vGPU/GPU-hour estimate.
3. Procurement action: if cloud capacity quota request required, submit to cloud-ops with lead time per provider (AWS typically 3-7 business days for large requests).
4. Execution: Terraform plan -> review -> apply in automation account using PRs and CI gating (see CI/CD section).

Cloud Accounts & Networking Conventions
--------------------------------------
- Account naming: redwood-<env>-gpu-<region> (e.g., redwood-prod-gpu-usw2).
- VPC CIDR assignment: Use centralized allocation registry (see appendix). Default: /16 per account, /20 per region-VPC. Avoid overlap with customer networks.
- Subnets: 3 AZs minimum; subnets for compute (private), management (private with NAT), and public for bastions.
- Transit and egress: Transit Gateway in shared-services routes to customer VPCs and hub security appliances. Egress must traverse firewall for policy/inspection.
- Peering and routing: Use Transit Gateway attachments not VPC peering for scale. Route tables annotated with tag: "redwood:route-purpose" with values [gpu-internal, management, external].

Security & IAM
--------------
- Principle of least privilege: automation account assumes a cross-account role with only terraform:Plan/Apply and iam:PassRole as scoped.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS keys in the account for volumes and secrets. Keys must have key policy that includes the security-audit role.
- Host isolation: GPU nodes run under dedicated instance profiles limiting S3 access. Any S3 access must go through a VPC endpoint and be restricted by IAM condition.

Terraform / IaC Modules (convention and examples)
------------------------------------------------
Core modules (in infra/modules):
- vpc (creates VPC, subnets, NAT, route tables)
- gpu-node-pool (provisions autoscaling group / instance fleet or node group for k8s)
- iam-roles (standardized service roles and cross-account roles)
- monitoring (CloudWatch/Prometheus exporters, dashboards)
- kms (key creation and grants)

Module usage example (recommended pattern):

1) Module invocation (root account repo):

```
module "gpu_vpc" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//vpc?ref=v1.12.0"
  account = "redwood-prod-gpu-usw2"
  region  = "us-west-2"
  cidr    = "10.40.0.0/16"
  azs     = ["us-west-2a","us-west-2b","us-west-2c"]
}
```

2) Node pool example (EC2 or k8s):

```
module "gpu_pool_m40" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//gpu-node-pool?ref=v1.6.2"
  vpc_id = module.gpu_vpc.vpc_id
  instance_type = "p4d.24xlarge"
  target_capacity = 40
  scaling_policy = {
    min = 10
    max = 200
  }
}
```

Recommended variables table (example):

| variable | type | default | description |
|---------|------|---------|-------------|
| account | string | - | AWS account id / logical name |
| region | string | us-west-2 | Region to provision |
| cidr | string | - | VPC CIDR block |
| instance_type | string | p3.8xlarge | Default GPU instance type |
| target_capacity | number | 10 | Desired GPU instance count |

Module versioning: pin module versions in root-level repo using tags (semver). Do not reference branch heads for production.

CI/CD and Build Conventions
---------------------------
Pipeline goals: safe, auditable infra changes; automated preflight checks; staged rollouts.

Pipeline stages (typical terraform repo):
1. PR + lint (tflint, checkov policy scans).
2. Plan (terraform plan in ephemeral container, plan file uploaded to artifact store).
3. Security scan (static IAM policy checks, terraform-graph based checks).
4. Manual approval for prod plans (via GitHub PR or dedicated approval tool).
5. Apply (automation pipeline assumes cross-account role and runs terraform apply using the approved plan).
6. Post-apply verification (sanity checks: instance counts, subnet allocation, monitoring alerts).

Gating and Safety
- All applies to prod require at least two reviewers with infra-team write privileges.
- Change windows: large capacity changes (>25% change in pool size) must be scheduled during a maintenance window unless emergency.
- Rollback: use terraform to revert to previous tag/commit and reapply. For stateful migrations, follow the Upgrade and Rollback section.

Build artifacts and registries
- Container images for terraform runners and custom providers are built by infra-ci and stored in ECR with tags matching commit SHA.
- State storage: encrypted S3 with DynamoDB state locking. State buckets named: redwood-terraform-state-<env>-<region>.

Runbooks (operational playbooks)
--------------------------------
Key runbooks (summaries below). See runbooks folder for expanded playbooks.

1) GPU pool scaling incident
- Symptoms: request queue latency climbs while node count remains constant, autoscaler failing to launch new nodes.
- Immediate actions:
  a) Check autoscaler logs and AWS EC2 LaunchFailures (Console + CloudWatch).
  b) Confirm quota and AZ capacity in account via AWS Support Console.
  c) If quota exhausted, escalate to cloud-ops and trigger pre-approved quota increase flow.
  d) If AMI or launch template invalid, rollback to previous template and trigger apply.
  e) If networking prevents provisioning, check subnet IP availability and TGW route propagation.
- Postmortem: runbook owner opens incident review and tracks RCA.

2) Network connectivity issue to shared services
- Symptoms: no egress to artifact S3/packaging registry or failure to reach control-plane endpoints.
- Immediate actions:
  a) Verify TGW attachments and route tables.
  b) Validate security appliance health (failover to standby if applicable).
  c) Re-route traffic temporarily to backup egress path.

Maintenance & Upgrade Windows
----------------------------
- Weekly small maintenance window: Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC for non-prod.
- Monthly production maintenance: First Sun 01:00-05:00 UTC.
- Major upgrades (kernel, AMI, large instance family changes) require 7-day pre-notice and canary rollout across 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%.

Upgrade and Rollback Guidance
----------------------------
1. Plan: create upgrade PR with exact module versions and migration steps.
2. Canary: apply to staging, then to a small prod pool (2% traffic) and monitor metrics for 24-72h.
3. Roll forward if stable; roll back by re-applying previous infra tag and performing any necessary in-service rollback steps (e.g., redeploy agent version).

Checklist for Major Change PRs
-----------------------------
- [ ] Impact analysis attached (capacity delta, risk matrix).
- [ ] Automated plan passed (no unexpected deletions).
- [ ] Security checks passed (IAM, KMS, network).
- [ ] Two infra reviewers and one security reviewer approved.
- [ ] Rollout plan and rollback steps documented.
- [ ] Communications sent to consumers (runtime/product) 48h prior.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Links
----------------------------------
- Terraform plan (example): `terraform init && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan`
- Apply with automation: `infra-ci apply --plan plan.tfplan --account redwood-prod-gpu-usw2`
- Check state bucket: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-terraform-state-prod-usw2/`
- Node pool health dashboard: Console -> Dashboards -> infra/gpu-node-pool-health
- Module repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-modules.git

Frequently Referenced Documents
-------------------------------
- infra-iac-modules-ci-cd-guidelines-2026 (module patterns and templates)
- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026 (detailed operational runbook)
- infra-gpu-fleet-capacity-and-iac-strategy-2025 (strategy and procurement notes)

Revision history
----------------
- 2025-11-20: Initial draft (Alex Martinez).
- 2026-03-04: Published with CI/CD and runbook consolidation; reviewers Priya Patel, Jordan Lee, Morgan Chen.

If you are onboarding: follow the Quickstart path in the infra repo (README.md) which walks through spinning up a staging VPC and a small GPU node pool using the example modules. For any gaps or questions, ping #infra-gpu on Slack or open a PR against this page for corrections.
